explained.tdh.how.meta.title: How TDH is calculated
explained.tdh.how.meta.description: Every step of the TDH v1.4 rules, each with a model you can move and break, and the exact rule beside it.
explained.tdh.how.title: How TDH is calculated
explained.tdh.how.lede: Every step of the TDH v1.4 rules, in four ideas: time, rarity, collections and you, each with a model you can move and break, and the exact rule beside it.
explained.tdh.how.parts.label: The four parts
explained.tdh.how.parts.a.title: Time
explained.tdh.how.parts.a.line: A day counts only when it is whole.
explained.tdh.how.parts.b.title: Rarity
explained.tdh.how.parts.b.line: Rarer cards count more per copy.
explained.tdh.how.parts.c.title: Collections
explained.tdh.how.parts.d.title: You
explained.tdh.how.parts.d.line: Up to four wallets count as one.
explained.tdh.how.a.title: A day counts only when it is whole.
explained.tdh.how.a.body: Once a day TDH takes a snapshot of Ethereum: the last block before {midnight}. A result is dated by its snapshot and counts the day before it. A copy adds one day for every whole {hours} hours it has been held at that snapshot.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.label: A card ages
explained.tdh.how.firstday.question: When does a copy start to count?
explained.tdh.how.firstday.guess: a copy arrives at {time} on {date}. Which result counts its first whole day?
explained.tdh.how.firstday.answer: {right}. The snapshot of {early} finds one minute; the snapshot of {right} finds {hours} hours and one minute. Two minutes later, at {later}, it would be {after}.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.aria: A timeline of four daily snapshots, the copy's arrival and the time it is held. {say}
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayFirst: The result dated {date} counts its first whole day ({held} held).
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayBefore: The one before found {held}: not a whole day.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.saySold: It left before a whole day: no result ever counts it, and the buyer starts from zero.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayNone: No result in this window counts it yet.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.ruleT: T = ts(B), the time of the last block before N × {day}
explained.tdh.how.firstday.ruleDrawn: drawn at midnight; T is a few seconds before it
explained.tdh.how.firstday.ruleSource: P26 §4.2, §4.3 · whole days, never parts of one
explained.tdh.how.eligible.label: Which cards count
explained.tdh.how.eligible.question: When does a new card start to count?
explained.tdh.how.eligible.pickGroup: Pick one of the newest cards
explained.tdh.how.eligible.aria: A timeline of daily snapshots after the first mint of {card}, {when}. The result dated {date} is the first that counts it.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.say: {card} was first minted {when}. The result dated {date} is the first whose snapshot finds that a whole day old; from then on the card counts, and a full set needs it.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.unavailable: The newest cards' first mints could not be read from 6529.io just now. The rule beside it stands, and Break it still runs.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.ruleNextGen: NextGen: minted at or before B
explained.tdh.how.eligible.ruleFirstMint: firstMint: the first mint, of any amount
explained.tdh.how.eligible.ruleSource: P26 §5.1. Mints are read as logged (§5), even one burned in the same transaction.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.break: mint and burn a copy {days} days early
explained.tdh.how.eligible.iLead: A small constructed input, from P26:
explained.tdh.how.eligible.iSetup: A holds {lateCopies} copies of Meme #{late}, first minted an hour before the snapshot. Y holds {earlyCopies} copies of Meme #{early}, minted {days} days before it. Into Meme #{early}'s mint transaction we insert a mint of {inserted} copy of Meme #{late}, and its burn.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.iCaption: Counterexample I, without and with the inserted mint and burn
explained.tdh.how.eligible.sayILead: Where the rule reads every mint.
explained.tdh.how.eligible.sayI: Every stack is the same, yet the inserted mint makes the card's first mint {days} days old, so it counts: H rises, and Y no longer holds a full set. Counterexample I of the Lean model; netting is proved for the stacks only.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.label: Sales and moves
explained.tdh.how.stacks.question: When you sell one of several copies, which one leaves?
explained.tdh.how.stacks.act.move: B moves its copy to A
explained.tdh.how.stacks.stackOf: {name}'s copies, the first in at the bottom
explained.tdh.how.stacks.linked: A and B are linked both ways: one identity, one card, two copies.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.sayHold: Each copy remembers when it arrived, and the identity adds both copies' days.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.saySell: The copy received last goes first: A's {fresh}-day copy leaves, and its days with it.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.sayMove: Inside one identity a move keeps a copy's age: B's {old} days arrive in A whole, on top of A's stack.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.sayBreak: Moved in last, B's {old}-day copy sits on top of A's stack, so A's sale takes it: {old} days leave, not {fresh}. 6529.io has always counted this way, and P26 keeps it.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleStack: stack[w] = arrival times, first in to last in
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleSell: send n: the last n entries leave
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleMove: same identity: they arrive with their times
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleOther: otherwise: n new entries, stamped now
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleRaw: raw = Σ days(a) over the stacks = {raw}
explained.tdh.how.stacks.ruleSource: P26 §7.1, §7.2. Last in, first out is the legacy order, and P26 keeps it on purpose.
explained.tdh.how.stacks.break: move B's copy to A, then sell one
explained.tdh.how.netting.label: Inside one transaction
explained.tdh.how.netting.question: If a copy leaves and comes back in one transaction, did it ever leave?
explained.tdh.how.netting.netSay: Nothing moved, so nothing is replayed.
explained.tdh.how.netting.stepsSay: Counted step by step, the copy leaves A and comes back new.
explained.tdh.how.netting.sayNet: TDH v1.4 replays each transaction's net movement only, so A's copy keeps its {days} days.
explained.tdh.how.netting.saySteps: the copy would restart at zero. TDH nets each transaction first (D131), so this does not happen.
explained.tdh.how.netting.hOne: A sends one copy of Meme #{m1} to C, and someone mints {n} copies of Meme #{m1} to X and burns them in the same transaction.
explained.tdh.how.netting.hTwo: Every net movement is the same with or without the mint and burn, so every stack is the same. But the card's minted count reads the logged steps: minted rises from {mintedBefore} to {mintedAfter}, H from {hBefore} to {hAfter}, the rate of Meme #{m2} from {rateBefore} to {rateAfter}, and B's TDH from {bBefore} to {bAfter}.
explained.tdh.how.netting.sayH: Netting is proved for the holding stacks only. A mint and its burn inside one transaction can still change other holders' TDH (counterexample H, a small constructed input). The pages say so wherever netting is claimed.
explained.tdh.how.netting.break: mint and burn in one transaction
explained.tdh.how.netting.ruleNet: net(w) = received − sent, in one transaction
explained.tdh.how.netting.ruleReplay: replay the pairs, never the steps
explained.tdh.how.netting.ruleMinted: §5 still counts every mint as logged
explained.tdh.how.netting.ruleSource: P26 §7.1, D131. The steps inside a transaction cannot change a stack; they can still change an edition.
explained.tdh.how.b.title: Rarer cards count more per copy, and every card adds about the same.
explained.tdh.how.b.body: A card's rate is {H} divided by its edition: {H} is FirstGM's edition, the largest, so FirstGM's rate is {rateFirstGM} and a {cap}-copy card's is {rate310}. A release that ends below {threshold} copies minted gets a final airdrop up to {cap}, so while fewer than {threshold} are minted a card counts as if it had its claim's limit, at most {cap}. From {threshold} on there is no top-up, and the minted count is the edition. No edition goes below {threshold}: that threshold is one of The Memes' two absolutes.
explained.tdh.how.rates.label: The rate and the edition floor
explained.tdh.how.rates.question: Why does a rare card earn more per copy, yet every card adds about the same?
explained.tdh.how.rates.sayFloor: Below {threshold} copies a card counts at its claim limit, up to {cap}, because the release tops it up to {cap}. Each copy adds {rate} a day; all {E} copies together add {area} a day, about the same as every other card.
explained.tdh.how.rates.say: each copy adds {rate} a day; all {E} copies together add {area} a day, about the same as every other card.
explained.tdh.how.rates.ruleSource: P26 §5.2, §8.1. A floor applies only below {threshold} minted; the {threshold} is locked (D89). Exact half cents round as P26 §8.1 says: see the {link}.
explained.tdh.how.base.label: Base TDH
explained.tdh.how.base.body: Each card's base TDH is its copies × whole days × rate, rounded to a whole number once per card in each wallet. Two copies of a {cap}-copy card held {days} days add {sum}, rounded to {rounded}. That rounding is why a move between your own linked wallets can change your total: by about a unit for each card moved, more with a boost.
explained.tdh.how.base.ruleSource: P26 §8.2: the rate in cents, rounded once per card in each wallet.
explained.tdh.how.c.title: One boost multiplies everything you hold.
explained.tdh.how.c.body: Each complete season adds {season}, once the next season has begun. A full set takes every complete season, plus a little for each further set. Genesis (#1 to #3) and Nakamoto (#4) add {single} each while the first season is not complete. Each 6529 Gradient adds {gradient}, up to {max}. Today's highest boost is about {todayMax}; the rule's ceiling is about {ceiling}, once season {last} is complete.
explained.tdh.how.boost.label: The boost ladder
explained.tdh.how.boost.question: What multiplies everything a collector holds, and where does it stop?
explained.tdh.how.boost.sayGrad: Gradients add {gradient} each, up to {max}; this one is a plain copy that earns its own rate.
explained.tdh.how.boost.saySets: A full set takes every complete season ({count} today), plus a little for each further set, never more than about {extra} in all.
explained.tdh.how.boost.saySingles: Genesis (#1 to #3) and Nakamoto (#4) count only while the first season is not complete.
explained.tdh.how.boost.say: One boost multiplies everything you hold. The newest season counts once the next one begins.
explained.tdh.how.boost.ruleSets: sets = the fewest copies of any card
explained.tdh.how.boost.ruleSetsOn: a full set: +{season} each paying season, + ADD(sets)
explained.tdh.how.boost.ruleSeasons: no full set: +{season} each complete season
explained.tdh.how.boost.ruleBeta: beta = the sum, rounded to the cent
explained.tdh.how.boost.ruleSource: P26 §8.3, §5.4. A season pays once the next one begins; every value is TDH v1.4's registry.
explained.tdh.how.d.title: Up to four wallets count as one collector.
explained.tdh.how.d.body: Wallets linked both ways become one identity. Their copies add up, the boost is computed once on everything they hold together, and copies moved between them keep their age. Your final TDH is each card's base times that one boost, rounded per card.
explained.tdh.how.d.link: How to link them, and why a number changes
explained.tdh.how.identity.sayLinked: Linked, A and B together hold all {count} cards of season {season}, so one boost of {boost} applies to every card.
explained.tdh.how.identity.sayApart: Apart, neither wallet completes the season, so neither has a boost: {a} and {b}, two separate collectors.
explained.tdh.how.identity.label: An identity
explained.tdh.how.identity.question: What changes when two wallets link?
explained.tdh.how.identity.sayOneWay: A pair groups only when both wallets register it. Until B signs too, A and B count apart, {a} and {b}, with no boost.
explained.tdh.how.identity.rulePair: pair = A → B and B → A, both registered
explained.tdh.how.identity.ruleBeta: beta = one boost on all it holds
explained.tdh.how.identity.ruleFinal: final = Σ FINAL(base, beta), card by card
explained.tdh.how.identity.ruleSource: P26 §6.2, §6.3, §7.3, §8.4. Which wallets group, and in what order, is D136's rule: Your wallets shows it.
explained.tdh.how.n.label: The network
explained.tdh.how.n.title: Today's total is the sum of {identities} identities.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyMore: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}, {delta} more than the day before.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyLess: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}, {delta} less than the day before.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyTotal: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}.
explained.tdh.how.n.cutover: About {date}, 6529.io moves to computing TDH with the Rust core, the program the daily check compares it with today.
explained.tdh.how.n.cutoverPast: 6529.io's move to computing TDH with the Rust core was planned for about {date}; as of {checked} it has not been made. The daily check cannot tell the two apart: the Rust core and the Python reference write the same records, byte for byte.
explained.tdh.how.n.unavailable: Today's totals could not be read from the daily comparison. The rules above do not depend on them.
explained.tdh.how.totals.label: Adding it up
explained.tdh.how.totals.question: What exactly is added to make the network's total?
explained.tdh.how.totals.caption: The records of the example identity: wallet A, wallet B and the identity they form
explained.tdh.how.totals.say: The identity's record counts once: every card's base times the identity's one boost, rounded card by card. The network's total adds every identity this way.
explained.tdh.how.totals.sayWallets: Each wallet record has its own boost, and wallet A alone does not complete the season. So the total adds identity finals; wallet finals are kept, never added.
explained.tdh.how.totals.ruleWallets: wallet finals: their own boost, never added
explained.tdh.how.totals.ruleSinks: also given without the burn addresses
explained.tdh.how.totals.ruleSource: P26 §7.3, §8.5. The burn addresses are identities of their own, and never link.
explained.tdh.how.order.label: All of it
explained.tdh.how.order.title: Every step, in the order P26 runs them.
explained.tdh.how.order.body: The four ideas above, set out as the specification computes a cycle. Each step links to the model that moves it.
explained.tdh.how.order.caption: The rules in P26's notation: {div} is whole-number division, {halfup} rounds a half up, and {b64} is the nearest double-precision value. The Specification restates every line in full.
explained.tdh.how.model.unavailable: This model needs the Meme editions from 6529.io, which could not be read just now.
explained.tdh.how.hwk.rulesBody: P26, TDH v1.4, §4 to §8 ({head}); restated in full on the Specification page.
explained.tdh.how.hwk.modelsBody: The TDH v1.4 engine, run in your browser. It passes {pass} of P26's {vectors} vectors, rerun in CI on every change.
explained.tdh.how.hwk.nettingBody: The Lean manifest, Netting invariance, and counterexamples H and I.
explained.tdh.how.hwk.decisionsBody: D89 (the {threshold} threshold), D131 (netting), D132 (the cutover), D136 (four wallets).
